findings.issue: The scene reference set covers only fit and inner rows. It omits scenes the models also read: val-cell rows (selection, kill criterion, conformal offsets), train-role 2022-23 rows, A1 context chips and SSL chips if that init is inherited. The choice changes the rule's outcome. With all dev rows as reference the preview falls below the 60% row threshold, so the roles would swap. The swap also makes the all-rows cell primary exactly when scene sharing is highest.

WQP 2015-2023 rows and context or SSL chips will lower every fraction further (l.130-131). Counts are on any-target rows; the binding rule uses the chl-a cell.
findings.suggested_ruling: The reference set is the scene keys of every chip read in fitting, early stopping, selection, calibration or pretraining of any arm or comparator (all non-protected non-buffer dev_v5m rows, their context chips, and the SSL manifest chips if that init is inherited); thresholds are unchanged; and when all rows are primary, a §15.1 label also requires the scene-disjoint estimate to favour the arm against every comparator.

findings.issue: The context rule does not require a context chip to share the row's split role, and it does not name the chip stores. For non-lake rows a chip "centred within 100 m" can belong to a different water body or block, so a train-role row could read imagery of a test-role site. Four stores exist; which ones count as "any existing chip store" is left open, and membership follows in-situ sampling.
findings.evidence: Amendment l.296-299: non-lake members are chips within 100 m; "Chips come from any existing chip store". Stores under processed/s2_chips: aquacorr, wqp, naip_teacher (10,694 index rows, rebuilt 2026-11-09) and mc_benchmark (5,924 rows). /home/bcheng/STOCKHOLM/SENTINEL-STOCKHOLM/sentinel/models/orbit/data.py STORES lists only aquacorr and wqp. Split v3 assigns a point within 500 m of a lake to that lake (split.py LAKE_MAX_DIST_M), so a non-lake row and a chip 100 m away can differ in water body and role. No count of affected rows was made: the context builder does not exist yet.
findings.suggested_ruling: A context chip must have the same frozen-rule water body and split role as its row (non-lake rows: same 200-km block, not in-lake, not buffer-excluded); the context stores are named explicitly by the lead and pinned by content hash at the first dev_v5m build; mc_benchmark and any store built later are excluded.

findings.issue: The trophic-chain baseline is fitted on MDN_B predictions for the same fit-cell rows MDN_B was trained on. Those in-sample predictions are cleaner than the out-of-sample ones it is applied to at test, which biases the fit and weakens the comparator the amendment itself expects to be strong for TP and TN. The stacking GBM already uses out-of-fold predictions.
findings.evidence: Amendment l.201-203: OLS "fitted on the fit cell, of the log target on the validation-selected MDN_B's predicted log chl-a and log Secchi"; no out-of-fold wording. Contrast l.362-364: the stacking GBM uses "out-of-fold predictions (5 folds grouped by role block within the fit cell)". No code exists yet for this baseline, so this is a reading of the text only.
findings.suggested_ruling: The trophic-chain OLS is fitted on out-of-fold MDN_B predictions (5 folds grouped by role block within the fit cell, as for the stacking GBM) and applied to the full-fit MDN_B predictions.

findings.issue: The 100 m same-date join of a WQP station to an AquaCorr row is not restricted to the same water body or role. A station assigned to another water body could give its value to a row of a different role. The 1,000 m buffer rule makes this rare.
findings.evidence: Amendment l.182-183: "the nearest WQP station within 100 m on the same date". For base targets the equivalent merge is inside dedupe (data.py l.212-244) before split assignment; the new join is a separate path that does not exist yet. Not measured: counting affected rows needs station-level split assignment for wqp_discrete sites, which I did not run.
findings.suggested_ruling: The 100 m join of §2.4 is made only to a WQP station whose frozen-rule water body equals the row's; otherwise the row carries no value for that target.

points.recommendation: Change. Use the stricter set: every non-protected, non-buffer dev_v5m row (fit, inner, val-role, train-role 2022-23), their context chips, and SSL manifest chips if that init is inherited. Keep both thresholds. Add the sign-agreement condition when all rows are primary.
points.reason: The choice decides which cell is primary. Keys-only preview: 69.5% disjoint with fit+inner, 63.4% with val-role rows added, 58.1% with all dev rows, which is below the 60% threshold before WQP 2015-2023 rows and context chips lower it further.

points.recommendation: Confirm, with the condition that the calculation reads validation predictions and protected counts only and that its script is named in the rulings.
points.reason: The existing method (orbit_power.py, protocol §5a) uses protected counts only; the rule and thresholds are already fixed in the text.

points.point: 3. Context date limit and two-sided context (§3.4 item 3)
points.recommendation: Confirm the <= 2023-12-31 limit and two-sided context, and add: context chips must share the row's water body and split role, and the chip stores are named and pinned now.
points.reason: The date limit keeps headline-year imagery out. The role and store gaps are the open leakage paths (F-CTX-ROLE).

points.recommendation: Confirm, and apply the same out-of-fold rule to the trophic-chain OLS.
points.reason: Out-of-fold predictions grouped by role block are the right guard against in-sample stacking; the OLS baseline lacks it (F-OLS-INSAMPLE).

points.point: 7. Shared initialisation fixed when A0 starts (§3.1)
points.recommendation: Change to a fixed cut-off: both arms use the non-SSL init unless chain9 has registered its selection by a date and time the lead writes into the rulings; the decision is logged in the registry before the first A0 network starts and is never revisited.
points.reason: "When A0 starts" is a moment the engineer controls and can pick after seeing chain9's interim validation numbers.

points.recommendation: Confirm separation outside the v1 globs, with three conditions: the v2 guard and loaders are independently reviewed before any dev_v5m build reads a new-target value; look tests use only a temporary runs root; a claim refuses a non-empty look directory.
points.reason: The v1 look list and freeze path are hard-coded, so M2S/test needs new guard code that does not exist yet, and a unit test has already written an abort marker into the real M2/test directory (F-ABORT-MARKER).

summary: Hash matches. No result exists on any new arm or Track N target; the counts script is keys-only; v1 guard paths behave as described. No blocking finding, but the stamp needs rulings. (1) M7's sealed look already scored an S2 SatWQ-Net at up to 106 site-dates in Test-S lakes, and the M7 national look would add more. (2) A pytest-written ABORTED.json in the real M2_test directory would spend M2/test at claim. (3) The scene reference set omits val, train 2022-23, context and SSL scenes; with all dev rows only 58.1% is disjoint, below the 60% threshold. (4) Two disclosed facts are missing from the file. (5) The v2 loaders do not exist yet and need review.
